blockers:
claim: C ABI integrity violation: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown are declared in the public C API but are now no-op functions that do nothing, breaking the contract that callers expect these functions to have observable effect. The documentation says 'init always returns ECUIO_OK' but doesn't explain what the functions actually do or guarantee.; file: core/include/ecuio/core.h; quote: ecuio_status_t ecuio_init(void);
 void ecuio_shutdown(void);

claim: Error propagation broken: The QML bridge previously used m_initialized to track whether ecuio_init succeeded. Now that ecuio_init is a no-op that always returns ECUIO_OK, the bridge has no way to know if initialization actually succeeded. The (void)ecuio_init() call discards the return value, eliminating error detection.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: (void)ecuio_init();   // optional and always ECUIO_OK (core.h), paired below
questions: What global state, if any, does the core module actually have that requires initialization? The removal of g_initialized suggests none, but the original code had it for a reason.
Are there any callers outside this repository that depend on ecuio_init having side effects (like initializing global resources, setting up logging, etc.)?
What happens if ecuio_init is never called and a session is created? Does the profile registry or discovery code handle this case correctly?
Is there any race condition in the profile registry initialization? The comment mentions 'C++11 magic statics' but I need to verify this is sufficient.
nits: The comment in core.h says 'init always returns ECUIO_OK' but should also document that the function does nothing (no side effects).
The comment in core.cpp could be clearer about why ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown are now no-ops.
Consider adding a deprecation notice or documentation explaining the lifecycle change for existing callers.
